fact_text: The Pakistan Stock Exchange and Meezan Bank launched the KMI 30 index in 2008 as a Shariah-compliant benchmark.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Your Stocks Are Probably Haram (Here's Why) | Shariah stocks' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The KMI All Share index, a Shariah-compliant benchmark also built by the PSX and Meezan Bank, was launched in 2015.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Your Stocks Are Probably Haram (Here's Why) | Shariah stocks' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: KSE 100 covers the top 100 listed companies, KMI 30 the top 30 Shariah-compliant ones, and KMI All Share every listed Shariah-compliant company.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Your Stocks Are Probably Haram (Here's Why) | Shariah stocks' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A 2014 committee of market bodies and Meezan Bank drafted the six Shariah screening criteria that still decide index membership.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Your Stocks Are Probably Haram (Here's Why) | Shariah stocks' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Under the business-activity screen, a company whose core business is prohibited, such as alcohol or non-halal meat, fails outright.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Your Stocks Are Probably Haram (Here's Why) | Shariah stocks' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Tobacco and explosives businesses are also excluded from the Shariah-compliant universe on ethical grounds.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Your Stocks Are Probably Haram (Here's Why) | Shariah stocks' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Murree Brewery makes alcohol among other products, so its core business fails the Shariah business-activity screen.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Your Stocks Are Probably Haram (Here's Why) | Shariah stocks' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Interest-bearing debt must be below 37% of total assets to pass the Shariah debt screen.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Your Stocks Are Probably Haram (Here's Why) | Shariah stocks' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Non-compliant investments, including interest-bearing bank deposits, must stay below 33% of total assets.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Your Stocks Are Probably Haram (Here's Why) | Shariah stocks' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Income from non-compliant sources must stay below 5% of total revenue to pass the screen.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Your Stocks Are Probably Haram (Here's Why) | Shariah stocks' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The screen requires illiquid assets, meaning assets that cannot be sold quickly, to exceed 25% of total assets.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Your Stocks Are Probably Haram (Here's Why) | Shariah stocks' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The market price per share should be at least equal to the net liquid assets per share, a technical valuation test in the screen.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Your Stocks Are Probably Haram (Here's Why) | Shariah stocks' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Companies on the defaulters counter or with trading suspended are excluded from the Shariah index lists.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Your Stocks Are Probably Haram (Here's Why) | Shariah stocks' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Mutual funds, whether open-ended or closed-ended, cannot be included in the KMI All Share index.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Your Stocks Are Probably Haram (Here's Why) | Shariah stocks' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Analysts at Almeezan review each listed company's financial reports on an ongoing basis and remove firms that breach the thresholds.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Your Stocks Are Probably Haram (Here's Why) | Shariah stocks' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: KMI indices are recomposed twice a year: the 15 May review uses data to 31 December of the prior year, and the 15 November review uses data to 30 June.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Your Stocks Are Probably Haram (Here's Why) | Shariah stocks' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The PSX website publishes each recomposition's incoming and outgoing companies, with the reason each outgoing company was dropped.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Your Stocks Are Probably Haram (Here's Why) | Shariah stocks' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: At the end of 2024, 271 of the 530 companies listed on the PSX were Shariah-compliant, about 51% of the count.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Your Stocks Are Probably Haram (Here's Why) | Shariah stocks' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: At the end of 2024, Shariah-compliant companies made up over 55% of total PSX market capitalisation.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Your Stocks Are Probably Haram (Here's Why) | Shariah stocks' (YouTube transcript, undated)
